intended_object: The evolution operator (propagator) of the non-autonomous linear ODE x'(t) = A(t)x(t) on a real Banach space: V t y s is the value at time t of the unique solution with x(s) = y. Inferred from the docstring and from IsFlowOn / existsUnique_linearFlowOn.
explanation: The body chooses the unique V : ℝ → E → ℝ → E with IsFlowOn (fun t z => A t z) V. IsFlowOn has two parts: the initial condition V s y s = y, and for all t, HasDerivAt (fun r => V r y s) (A t (V t y s)) t. Its existence and uniqueness are the library's theorem existsUnique_linearFlowOn, so Classical.choose picks out a canonical object: the global two-parameter solution operator U(t,s)y. The setting is a real Banach space with A continuous into E →L[ℝ] E. This is the standard generality for linear non-autonomous ODEs: completeness is needed for existence and time is real. I don't know of a Mathlib definition of this propagator; I did not search Mathlib for one. The definition matches its docstring and the standard notion.
